_doc: FOREIGN IDENTIFIER BUDGET — every DECLARED IDENTIFIER of the repository that an ENGLISH-ONLY dictionary refuses, DECLARED with its class. SINGLE SOURCE, consumed by `test/foreign-identifier-gate.test.js` through `src/foreign-identifier-pure.js`. DETECTION is NOT here: it lives in `rules/declared-identifier.yml` (ast-grep, WHERE the names are) and in `cspell.json` (WHICH words are English). Strict separation — the rule detects with zero exemption, this file plus its test carry the POLICY and the RATCHET. Same shape as the quadratic, temporal and state-entry-rebuild twins; never invent another one.
_doc_why: This repository is PUBLIC and its language decision says the WHOLE project is English. The PROSE half already had a machine (`english-only-gate.test.js`, scope `docs/framework/`). The IDENTIFIERS had NONE, and French ones shipped in the published repository — `verrou`, `chemin`, `voiePrete`, `docsFantomes`, `morceau`. A reader who cannot read the identifiers cannot read the code, and no contributor can extend a vocabulary they do not understand.
_doc_inverted_burden: 🛑 THE DESIGN DECISION, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT: there is NO list of forbidden French words. A list of FORBIDDEN things is stale the day it is written — it catches only what somebody thought to put in it, and the next word walks through in silence; that defect class has already been paid for here. `cspell` INVERTS THE BURDEN OF PROOF: nothing is forbidden, what is KNOWN is declared (ordinary English plus the house terms of `cspell.json`), so every other word is RED. A German `dateipfad`, a Portuguese `caminho` and a French `verrou` are refused for exactly the SAME reason — they are not English. That covers the languages nobody anticipated, which no list can do. Fail-closed, never fail-open. The contributors of this repository are international: the next offending identifier will not necessarily be French.
_doc_english_only: 🛑 AND THAT GUARANTEE RESTS ON ONE FACT ALONE: ENGLISH IS THE ONLY NATURAL-LANGUAGE REFERENCE. Enabling one additional natural-language dictionary opens THAT WHOLE LANGUAGE in silence and the gate stops protecting without a single test going red. `dictionaries` below is therefore an EQUALITY on what cspell says it ACTUALLY loaded — the config is made to SPEAK, never trusted — plus a shape refusal on any dictionary named like a locale that is not English. A configuration nobody made speak is not a verified configuration.
_doc_scope: DECLARED IDENTIFIERS ONLY — variables, parameters, functions, classes, object-literal keys, methods, destructured bindings. NEVER prose: a French word in a COMMENT or a STRING is a FALSE POSITIVE by construction here (this repository's comments quote defects verbatim, and French sentences live inside `english-only-gate.test.js` as detector fixtures). That is why detection is AST and never regex. Uses are excluded too: a member access is not a place where somebody CHOSE a word, and flagging it would report one rename as a hundred reds.
_doc_blind_spot: 📐 DECLARED BLIND SPOT, MEASURED 2026-08-24 AND WRITTEN RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The English dictionary contains FRENCH LOANWORDS, so a French identifier that is also an English word is INVISIBLE to this gate. Measured on 25 probed French words: 9 pass — chemin, morceau, parc, nom, sortie, dedans, sain, garde, dossier. That is a property of ANY dictionary-based approach, not a bug of this one, and it is the price of the inverted burden of proof: the alternative (a hand-written list of French words) would catch those nine and MISS every language nobody anticipated, which is strictly worse. 🛑 The remedy is NOT to add those words to a forbidden list — it is that such names were renamed by hand in the same gesture as the gate (chemin→filePath, parc→fleet, nom→itemName, morceau→chunk…), and that a reviewer knows the gate does not cover them. A witness of this gate must therefore NEVER use a loanword: two of them (chemin, morceau) were chosen first and the ANTI-INERT cell caught it, which is exactly what witnesses are for.
_doc_keys: A BUDGET KEY IS A RELATIVE PATH, NEVER A BASENAME. This repository holds homonyms across `src/`, `src/sources/`, `src/hooks/`, `tools/` and `test/`: two of them melted into one key would make the red NON-ACTIONABLE — one would know a foreign name is undeclared without knowing in WHICH file. Paths use forward slashes on every OS.
_doc_baseline: 📐 BASELINE GENERATED BY MEASUREMENT OF THIS REPOSITORY ON 2026-08-24, never copied from elsewhere: 217 tracked JavaScript files, 17,610 declared identifiers, and 888 foreign occurrences over 508 distinct identifiers in 138 files BEFORE the rename. The renaming brought that to the `files` map below. An empty map is not an unset gate: a file absent from `files` is held at ZERO, so every foreign identifier written from now on is RED on sight. The recipe is shared across the fleet; the NUMBERS are not — an imported figure would be an INVENTED ratchet, and an invented ratchet protects nothing.
_doc_noise: 📐 THE NOISE WAS MEASURED BEFORE THE GATE WAS TRUSTED, because a noisy gate gets disarmed and this repository knows it. Over the WHOLE TEXT of the 217 tracked JavaScript files (prose, strings and identifiers together) cspell rejected 935 distinct words in 4,690 places — unusable, and mostly comments quoting defects on purpose. Restricted to DECLARED IDENTIFIERS the same run rejected 508 distinct names in 888 places, of which the overwhelming majority were genuinely French. The AST perimeter is what turns an unusable measurement into an actionable one.
_doc_classes: CLOSED list. `PROTOCOL_NAME` = the identifier REPRODUCES a name we do not own (a third party's environment variable, a wire-format field, a vendor API key): renaming it would break a contract outside this repository. An act of instruction, so a written `why` is REQUIRED. `DEBT` = a foreign identifier knowingly kept: it owes a `why` AND a NUMERIC `impact` naming who reads it, because a budget measures QUANTITY and never GRAVITY. `INHERITED_DEBT` = the measurement of the day, EXEMPT from justification ON PURPOSE — nobody has instructed those cases one by one, and demanding a sentence would produce INVENTED ones, which would then make the case look settled. A false justification is worse than none.
_doc_ratchet: The declared `max` must EQUAL the measured count. Measured ABOVE = a new foreign identifier appeared: rename it in English, or prove the class — 🛑 NEVER raise the `max` to make a push go through. Measured BELOW = a STALE declaration: LOWER IT in the same gesture, otherwise the ground gained is silently taken back by the next writer, who inherits the old ceiling. A declaration with no occurrence left is a DORMANT PERMIT and is RED: that is how an exemption which has stopped being necessary reddens instead of rotting.
_doc_exit: EXIT CONDITION of the whole file: zero entry of any kind. A foreign identifier leaves the budget by being RENAMED, never by widening the ratchet. 🛑 AND IT NEVER LEAVES BY BEING ADDED TO `cspell.json`: a technical term of the domain belongs in `words`, a FOREIGN identifier is RENAMED. Putting one in `words` disarms the gate while looking like configuring it — the single way this machinery can be misused, and it is invisible once done.
_doc_floors: ANTI-VACUITY — a gate that analyses nothing goes green, this repository's worst defect class, already paid for three times. Two floors, because they fail differently: the PERIMETER catches a `git ls-files` that came back empty or ran from the wrong directory, and the IDENTIFIER count catches an ast-grep invocation that resolved nothing (it returns an EMPTY JSON with EXIT 0 on a path it cannot resolve, so a misresolved perimeter is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a clean repository). Both sit deliberately far below the measurement: they catch a BLIND scan, they are not a second ratchet.
_doc_dictionaries: THE ACTIVE DICTIONARY SET, MEASURED FROM CSPELL ITSELF on 2026-08-24 (`cspell dictionaries --config cspell.json`, starred = active), never assumed. All fourteen are English or purely technical. The gate demands EQUALITY with what cspell reports: a dictionary appearing tomorrow — including one pulled in by an inherited or machine-global configuration nobody wrote here — is RED until somebody declares it and states it carries no natural language but English; a declaration whose dictionary has vanished is RED too.
_doc_witnesses: ANTI-INERT, the guarantee that holds everything else. Every ATOM of `rules/declared-identifier.yml` — one declaration site — is DERIVED from the `.yml` and MUST be paired here with a real line of code whose detection is REQUIRED (written to the OS tmpdir, run through the WHOLE pipeline, detection asserted). An atom without a witness is REFUSED, so an atom added tomorrow stays RED until someone proves it sees anything at all; a witness for an atom that no longer exists is RED too, because a stale witness silently inflates the appearance of coverage. 🔴 It is not ceremony: `ast-grep` returns an EMPTY JSON with EXIT 0 on a path it cannot resolve, and the tmpdir is used rather than a folder of the repository because `ast-grep` HONOURS `.gitignore` — witnesses written into an ignored folder are invisible and every atom would be wrongly cleared. Each witness carries a FOREIGN name on purpose: it proves BOTH halves of the pipeline in one gesture, the AST locating the name and cspell refusing it.
